description: Review generated assets: set verdict (accepted|rejected|pending), selected and/or defect tags. Pass ONE id, or `ids` for a bulk review — after a generation run there are usually dozens to sort, and clicking through them one by one is why the review fields went unused. Rejected assets drop out of the default listings and become prunable. Note: single-id calls make `selected` exclusive per scene (one chosen variant per scene_ref); bulk calls do NOT, because a bulk over one scene would keep resetting itself and only the last id would stay selected. To record WHAT is wrong, pass `tags` (see the field) — with or without a verdict; a call with only `tags` changes no verdict. Tags are written after the verdict: if the tags fail, the verdict stays saved and the answer says so under `tags_error`. Bulk tagging is not available on a device grant.

id.description: Single asset id (positive integer as string). Use this for the per-scene selection

ids.description: Many asset ids for a bulk review (max 200). Mutually exclusive with `id`

reason.description: Why — stored as verdict_reason, useful when reviewing a rejection later

reference_type.description: What kind of asset these ids refer to

tags.description: Defect tags: WHAT is wrong, from a fixed list — independent of the verdict (an accepted asset can carry tags; tags never change verdict or selected). At most 5 per asset. Pass only tags that apply to the asset type (the brackets show where each applies). action_wrong [video/image] — a requested action does not happen or happens differently (also ambient movement such as shadows, lights, crowds); expression_wrong [video/image] — facial expression, gaze or blinking is wrong; camera_motion [video] — the camera moves differently from the request (handheld shake or push-in missing, wrong direction); framing [video/image] — shot size, angle, horizon or position in the frame differs from the request; colour_shift [video/image] — colour or light differs from the request or jumps; wrong_count [video/image] — wrong number of people or things (e.g. fewer extras than asked); missing_element [video/image] — a requested object or detail is not there; identity_drift [video/image] — face, wardrobe or build differs from the reference; wrong_place [video/image] — the place or layout does not match; anachronism [video/image] — something from the wrong era in a period setting; extra_people [video/image] — a person who is not part of the cast; text_wrong [video/image] — requested text is wrong or unreadable; anatomy [video/image] — hands, limbs or face are distorted; artifacts [video/image] — flicker, distortion, watermark, logo or a visible seam; frozen [video] — the picture freezes; continuity_jump [video] — the join at a cut or chained clip jumps; lip_sync [video] — lips do not match the sound; audio_wrong [video/sound] — sound is missing, jumps or does not fit; other [video/image/sound] — anything else — put the detail in `reason`.

tags_mode.description: add (default): add to the tags this person already set on the asset. replace: set exactly these tags (an empty list clears them). Only the caller's own tags are touched, never another person's or the machine tags.

verdict.description: Acceptance verdict. Feeds the acceptance telemetry (which provider/mode/price actually produced usable shots)
